title: Cupertino Mirror — iOS Settings Bento
description: A slide built around the visual grammar of Apple's Settings app — grouped rounded-rectangle cell lists, SF Symbol squircle icons, and a system-gray canvas — transplanted from phone to deck without sacrificing a pixel of HIG fidelity.
philosophy: This template exists for speakers who need to present mobile UX, app architecture, or privacy flows using the exact visual language their audience already navigates daily. It refuses the generic 'device mockup screenshot' approach, instead treating the grouped list cell as the atomic unit of composition: one idea, one icon, one label, one chevron. Decoration is the system itself. The status bar and device frame are not chrome — they are authority signals that tell a technical audience this presenter thinks in platforms.
goodFor: App feature walkthroughs structured around Settings-style navigation hierarchies
Privacy and permission setting explanations in product or compliance decks
iOS platform design critiques and Apple HIG deep-dives
Developer conference slides demoing mobile UI patterns to technical audiences
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews needing large data surfaces
Abstract brand storytelling or emotional campaign presentations
Large auditorium screens where 6-cell mobile detail reads as illegible noise
Non-tech audiences with no mental model of iOS navigation conventions
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide channels the quiet authority of an iOS Settings root screen — stillness, every element placed with platform-level precision. Mood is calm-technical: no decorative gradients, no editorial geometry — just the grouped cell and squircle icon as the sole compositional actors. Rhythm is sparse and centered, generous negative space framing the hero glyph so it reads as a trusted, familiar app icon. Avoid skeuomorphic shadows or any motif that competes with the system's own visual grammar.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid, centered spine; content stacks vertically in cols 3–10: a full-bleed status-bar strip pinned to the top edge signals iOS chrome authority, followed by a single oversized squircle icon as the hero glyph at roughly one-quarter canvas height, then the title text, then the subtitle housed in a compact grouped-cell capsule separated by a hairline divider that echoes a Settings section footer. Outer margins hold at 8% per side to preserve the phone-screen spatial feel. No page number; the status-bar strip serves as the sole top anchor.

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a real iOS Settings screen lifted intact onto a projection surface — grouped cells on a system-gray canvas radiating quiet institutional authority. Compositional rhythm is dense-modular: tight vertical cadence within each group, generous breathing between groups and at canvas edges. Each cell is a self-contained unit of meaning, never decorative. Avoid anything that reads as a generic 'presentation slide' — no illustrative flourishes, no asymmetric hero layouts, nothing that breaks platform fidelity.

examples.layoutNotes: Content slide uses a centered phone-width column (cols 3–10 of a 12-col grid) with an 8% outer margin on all sides. Two to three grouped rounded-rectangle cell stacks are arranged vertically, each preceded by an all-caps section-header label above the group boundary. Each cell row is a fixed-height strip: squircle icon flush left, label text center-left, disclosure chevron flush right. No deck header band or page-number footer intrudes — the device frame itself supplies the authoritative chrome.
